chapters.title: Chapter 1301: Clearing The Void Forest
paragraphs: The moment the demonic human died, the flag fell, and Kent caught it. However, before he could examine it, a powerful primal energy washed over the forest, causing all beasts to turn in his direction.
The energy came from the void temple, showing that the temple master of annihilation has reached his breaking point and, as such, wants Kent dead.
Every last horror hidden inside the forest stirred, and even those surrounding the temple left to go hunt down the bastard who seemed to enjoy slaughtering them.
"I guess I will handle this later." He stored away the flag, and then he extended his hand, summoning Gaap again.

While inside the flag, he knew using the sword would have limited him. As good as it may sound, facing immortals with his Sword King talent is not enough, even if the sword king in question is the reincarnation of the father of swordsmen.
He may have Heavenly Sword Aura and intent, but that isn’t enough. If he were to have his own sword realm, then at least he would have had a good run.

So abandoning his sword was the right move. But he is not inside the flag now, and as such, Gaap had to come back so they could commit the greatest massacre in their life... at least so far in their journey.
It was a wild series of massacres inside the Damned Hell sea, but this one would be on another level.
"Here we go." The Jade Void wings buzz, and he moves with speed blindingly.
Kent limited the number of flame veins to just 50,000, but if one were to see the speed at which he was moving, they would probably only see a blur and a splash of blood filling the air.
Kent took the tower’s decision, and so he decided not to waste time and instead farm for some blood essence and blood while Gaap went for the resentful souls.
The endgame is always to have more blood essence on hand when he needs it. So he went all out, and the result couldn’t be any more chilling.
In less than ten minutes, he had cleared the entire battlefield, and then he turned to the rest of the forest.
Kent is already aware that the forest will have to be cleared once he is done with the Void Temple. But that would be the work of the warriors on Planet Bayla.
Naturally, since he had no plans to waste precious blood, he chose to do it himself.
Five days quickly passed, and in those five days, Kent had not for one moment slowed down. He was on the move, killing everything he met.
Looking at the bloodthirsty aura coming off his body as he moved, one could tell his killing intent had reached a new level.
Even it could be seen in his eyes. They are crimson, and faint smoke continues to emanate from them as he moves. With every beast he kills, the bloodthirsty aura seems to increase.
By the close of ten days, what could have taken hundreds of thousands of warriors and a lot of casualties was accomplished by Kent. He had completely slaughtered every last beast.
Watching blood dripping off his sword, staring coldly down at a spider demon, Kent let a sigh escape his lips.
He raised his head and let out yet another sigh.
Then he deactivated the Jade Void wings, his horn, and his claws.
He sat in a lotus posture and closed his eyes.

The amount of bloodlust assaulting his mind, if not paid attention to, would affect him in the upcoming battles. So with no danger in sight, he sat down and let the passing of the hours help him calm down.
After three more days, he regained his sanity. However, his killing intent had reached a whole different level of danger.
"Tower, what changed with me?"

[Aside from the fact that the master had farmed millions in blood essence, the master had also levelled up his Heaven Sword Aura and intent to Level 9, and even better, the master’s killing intent had transcended beyond insanity.]
"I suppose I went wild, huh?" Kent smiled, feeling his blood boiling like crazy. The bloodlust is still there, just shimmering beneath the surface, waiting to be unleashed.
"Do I even have to have my Blood Cleansing Bath now?"
[The master must have the Blood Cleansing Bath. However, to be on the safer side, the master must do that inside the Void Temple.]
"I also think that is the best move. Better to be in a place I can cause the most damage than out here. Who knows what would become of me when I come out of the Blood Cleansing Bath?"

The first time he had that bath, Vexthra had to step in and save his skin. If not for her knocking him unconscious, he would have caused chaos inside the tower cities. Who knew how many he could have killed that day?

So, entering the Void Temple before doing that is indeed the best bet. If anything were to go wrong, he would just use the bloodlust to his advantage and trash the unlucky temple master who would stand in his way.
"I must absorb the blood essence now. The earlier I clear the temple, the better I can focus on other things. I still have three beasts to hunt for their fangs, so no time to waste."
[That is indeed true. The master has more than enough to saturate both cores and has surplus blood essence for other tasks.
But aside from that, I managed to extract 19 corrupted blood essence from the battle fought inside the flag. That is enough to refine nine Blood Life Seals and ten Blood Death Seals.]

"That is good news, but I will need about four years to refine and absorb all nineteen. That is just too long for me. So I will focus on only my cores. When I am back inside the tower, I will do that.
Of course, if you can leave a marker here, then I would enter the tower and handle that and return to take care of the Void Temple."
[Unfortunately, with the seal in place and the corruption in the air, I can’t do that. The master would have to depend on the passing of time outside, this time around.]

"Then I will focus on the Blood Essence. I want to be able to run circles around the temple masters. Back during the Primordial Era, Chaos always had the upper hand. That was why they hated him the most.
This time around, I want them to do more than hate me. I want them to fear me, for I will be their worst nightmare."
Kent snapped his finger, and ice burst from the ground, creating a cave-like fortress for him.

"Gaap, stay on the outside just in case we miss a target." Gaap transformed into his demon form and gave Kent a nod. He moved out and sat calmly atop the forest, his eyes closed, resentment emanating from him.
Back inside the forest, Kent waved his hand, and the air turned golden. Millions of blood essence appeared, filling the ice fortress with the aura of blood.
"Here we go." Kent formed a hand seal and began absorbing the blood essence at a speed that would shock anyone walking the blood path.
This time, he was merely saturating his cores, so he went all out, and the results soon began to show within minutes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1302: Cores Saturated
paragraphs: [14 Days Later]
A while back, when Kent formed the second blood core, he was shocked to find his first core had again increased in size, further demanding more blood essence to saturate it.
He had once saturated it to the max, hoping that was all. However, forming the second core revealed a bitter truth: each new core causes the old ones to grow much larger.
Obviously, of the many things he expected, he didn’t see that coming.
The idea of having to farm more blood essence to saturate both cores sounded like a hectic task he knew would take too much time to focus on.
His cores aren’t exactly the average size. They are enormous, and this is evident from the sheer amount of blood essence required to create and saturate them.

Sadly, it also means that whenever he wants to form a new core, the resources he would use would be more than those he used in previous ones. Basically, the more cores he forms, the more time and resources he would need.
Not forgetting the time he would have to invest into every last one of his cores.
However, now standing on the Blood Platform, gazing at the Blood Core Gates housing his two cores, he knew it was worth it.
Both cores had been fully saturated. Millions of golden runes line the surface of the cores, each releasing waves of energy that aren’t exactly something someone of Kent’s strength should be able to.
However, he understood that with his cores saturated, all he had to do was ascend to an immortal world, and his chance of reaching the Root Immortal stage was very high.
But that is in the future. The focus is now more on his gains, since a lot has changed after saturating both cores.
Surprisingly, he was able to reform his soul into a body, allowing him to physically interact with his Soul Sea. At first, he could only see inside his soul sea but could not walk around.
Now, gazing at the vast soul sea, made completely of a sea of blood, he couldn’t help but let a smile form on his face.
Kent had already been into the Primordial Spaces of his wives, and what he saw told him the kind of power they commanded.

Alina had runes and arrays everywhere, showing her nature as a formation expert. Elaine had half her Primordial Space full of life, and the other half filled with tombstones and a rather dried-up, horrible tree expressing her control over life and death.

Basically, everything about their Primordial Space, which to them represents their Soul Sea, reflected their job classes and talents. So for him to have a world of blood, Kent couldn’t help but click his tongue.
"The day I awaken my Primordial Spirit and Primordial Space, I will be sure not to bring the ladies here. I will basically be scaring them silly."
Kent didn’t know how, but aside from the churning sea and thunderstorm brewing in the air, the eeriness seemed to have reached a whole different level.
It was like his soul sea had become a blood-infested region where danger and blood are but one.
The blood sea stretched as far as the eye could see, and the Blood Platform on which the Blood Gates stood covered a rather large portion of the blood sea.
He had only formed two cores, so there are only two Core Gates standing on the platform. They stood tall and imposing. Each gate stood over 10,000 km tall and 5,000 km wide.
The cores themselves are akin to giant blood moons, filling the gates.
In fact, since the flame core is also occupying the first Blood Gate, that one looks even more dangerous.
There is a red core filled with blood hanging at the top and a green core radiating intense heat below it. The blood core is larger than the flame core, but the difference isn’t by much.
However, since they are both dangerous to even look at, Kent pays them less attention, oblivious to their true nature yet, and focuses on the new things that have appeared in his Soul Sea.
Quite a few scary and beautiful things had appeared inside the Soul Sea, and so he decided to focus on them instead.

The first is the large, horrific gate standing not too far from the Blood Platform. It is about 5,000 km tall and 2,500 km wide. The doors are huge and open in the middle, spreading both ways. On those enormous metallic doors, drawings—or more like carvings—of terrible-looking demonic beasts littered their rough surface.

"The Underworld Soul River Door." Kent didn’t need the tower to tell him what the door is. The latest soul skill—Underword Soul River—that he was too scared to use seemed to have manifested inside his Soul Sea.
When he tried to use it a couple of weeks after receiving it, Kent saw only a small opening into the terrifying sea hidden behind those doors.
That sight scared him so much that he chose to hold back his curiosity and let sleeping dogs lie. However, he knew he would have to use it at some point.
When that time comes, this terrifying door would manifest on the outside and open for all to witness the horror of the ’Underworld Soul River’.
"I should probably prepare mentally for this and, if possible, add more soul-strengthening cultivation techniques to the list. This way, I wouldn’t be too shaken by my own skill."
After Kent was done scrutinising the terrifying door, he shifted his attention to the second thing.
It is a large, 13-layered golden metallic disc with a mysterious aura around it. It has an intricate design, one that makes it look more like a cultivation diagram.

Kent had no idea what it was. However, he knew it was connected to him. He can tell it is important to him. But since he had no idea what it was, he planned to wait for now and search for understanding later.
"Maybe it is connected to my 13 reincarnations." Kent turned away, not willing to dwell on something he had no idea what. The next item, however, is a single circular red disc with six orbs.
Kent knew this one was linked to him somehow, too. However, he knew their true nature would be revealed when he finally met all six True Primordials and inherited their legacies.
It has six orbs representing the Six True Primordials, who are meant to lead Kent to the realm they could never reach. Becoming a True Primordial is Kent’s ultimate goal.
So seeing six orbs, he knew they were connected to it. This also means, just like the 13-layered disc, he would have to put it aside and focus on what he can handle right now.
Naturally, Kent didn’t mind examining them some more. However, he would only do that if he were inside the tower, where time is on his side.
So while he is setting them aside for now, he knew he would have to come back to them once he is done with his quest.
He turned to the last thing that suddenly appeared after saturating his two cores.

Kent turned to a majestic green tree that houses thousands of apple-looking golden fruits. Each fruit has hundreds of runes shimmering on its surface; however, only two seem to be ripe and are reddish.
"Tower, what am I looking at?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1303: Bloodline Skill Tree
paragraphs: Forget about the name of the tree; its appearance is everything. It has broad leaves and many interlocking branches, a cosy feel and a pleasant smell despite standing at the centre of a blood sea.
The leaves had been woven so intricately that they formed a perfect canopy, a perfect resting place after a long and hard day’s work, if this were a physical tree.
It is just magical and extremely beautiful.
Then there are the thousands of golden fruits hanging from the branches. They look edible, but at the same time, poisonous. Perhaps that was a sign for Kent not dare try eating it.
The two ripe ones stood out, giving the tree a unique aesthetic. Those ones, Kent could already sense the edible smell coming from them.

[This is the Bloodline Skill Tree. It is something of a myth, rumoured to have existed only among the Six True Primordials. It houses all the bloodline skills there are, and learning those skills is as simple as eating a fruit.]
"Hold on a minute, Tower." Kent took a deep gulp and slowly processed what Tower had said. He needed his clarity for what he was about to digest.

"You mean to say this tree standing before me, with over five thousand fruits on its branches, is a tree holding all the innate bloodline abilities I can awaken and use simply by eating mere ripped fruits?"
[Among other things, yes.]
"Among other things?" Kent gave the tower the "hold it there, girl" stance and asked, "Is there something else hidden that I should know?"
[As a matter of fact, yes. While the master is not yet aware, a person, no matter how monstrous, can have no more than 500 innate bloodline skills. Not even True Primordials had more than that...]
Kent looked at the Bloodline Skill Tree and counted over 5,000 fruits, meaning he has over 5,000 innate bloodline skills he can learn the moment the fruits are ripe.

If he were to take what Tower had just said into consideration, then it might seem he had just broken the innate bloodline ability scale by awakening the potential to unlock over 5,000 innate bloodline skills.
That is just mind-blowing, and he is well aware of that.
Unless, of course, there is something hidden beneath the surface. Naturally, Kent immediately unearthed that something.
"I am guessing this many fruits have something to do with my many reincarnations and the Six True Primordials."

[Yes, Master. The master had lived 13 lives, so it seems all innate talents linked to those lives have now manifested in this Bloodline Skill Tree, and as such, the master can learn them all by eating the ripe fruit.

Of course, the master may see it as too many innate skills considering the many fruits. After all, once one keeps growing in the path of ascension, the skills they learned as mortals would become ineffective when they become immortals.
This means they would be forced to learn stronger ones. However, the master shouldn’t worry since bloodline skills aren’t graded like external techniques.
These ones grow with the bloodline, so the stronger the bloodline becomes, the more advanced the skills. In other words, learning an innate skill today is for life.

Also, an innate bloodline skill can evolve other learned innate skills, transforming them into something else. So it can be that you will only learn 100 skills from this tree, but the others would superimpose on those 100 learned skills, making them more advanced and extremely powerful.]

"Well, when you put it that way, I guess I have not only become more powerful now, knowing I have a skill tree standing inside my Soul Sea, but I have the potential to learn over 5,000 innate bloodline skills."

Kent giggled like a child, feeling very happy he had landed this opportunity. It is indeed a great opportunity for someone like him. At this rate, worrying about learning other skills won’t be a problem.
It is as simple as plucking a fruit from a branch and eating it. What could be easier than that?
He wouldn’t have to find a stronger version of a skill after the previous one had become less effective. With just one, he could do more.
Kent keeps smiling; however, he suddenly furrowed his brow as if something important had just crossed his mind.
"Hold on a minute, Tower. You said this is a Bloodline Skill Tree, right? That I will awaken bloodline-related skills.
You also said that this tree houses all the innate bloodline skills tied to my many lives and those of the Six True Primordials.
If that is the case, does it mean I would have to awaken all 13 bloodlines and the six bloodlines that once belonged to the Six True Primordials before I can use them?"
Kent knew there had to be a catch.
If a skill is tied to one’s bloodline, then since he only has the Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline, does that mean he is only limited to the skills tied to that bloodline?
Obviously, he is missing something. There is no way he would be given something only to lock it away from him due to an error.

[The master is the Chaos Dragon, and he would always be the Chaos Dragon. This means he would only ever have the Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline. However, that doesn’t mean the master wouldn’t be able to wield other bloodline skills.]
"How?"
[The master didn’t ask, so I said nothing. However, the 13-layered discs and the six-orb disc, I believe, are connected to this skill tree.
The first one is called the 13 Layered Life Discs, which requires Life keys to unlock its power. I believe the master would obtain those by reviewing all the memories of his past lives.
The second one is the Six Mark Fate Disc. For that, the master would have to ask any of the True Primordials when he meets them again.]
And that answered his questions. It seems, aside from his bloodline, there are other ways to harness the bloodline abilities of other incarnations and even the True Primordials.

That seems convenient for him, meaning he would now have to figure out what he had to do to unlock the 13 discs. But for now, just knowing there is a way to harness those innate bloodline abilities is enough.
So far, aside from the [Chaos Aura] and [Chaos Dragon Scale] bloodline skills he had awakened, he is basically a brute without any refined skills to tap into when using his dragon form.
He had also forgone the use of the [Blood Chaos Aura] for now since he knew from Chaos that using that mutated aura would largely depend on his [Chaos Heart], which he had yet to form.
So in reality, he needs more skills tied to his bloodline than anything else. ’I wonder if by now walking the Blood & Slaughter path, my bloodline would also undergo mutation?’
Kent reeled in his emotions and chose to find out the answer himself.
It is always good if the results speak for themselves.
"I guess the next logical thing to do is eat these fruits and see what I would be getting this time around."
[That is true. The master must handle that. We, after all, still have temple masters to kill and more missions to go on.]
"Okay then," Kent reached and plucked one of the ripe fruits.

sentences.text: Forget about the name of the tree; its appearance is everything.
It has broad leaves and many interlocking branches, a cosy feel and a pleasant smell despite standing at the centre of a blood sea.
The leaves had been woven so intricately that they formed a perfect canopy, a perfect resting place after a long and hard day’s work, if this were a physical tree.
It is just magical and extremely beautiful.
Then there are the thousands of golden fruits hanging from the branches.
They look edible, but at the same time, poisonous.
Perhaps that was a sign for Kent not dare try eating it.
The two ripe ones stood out, giving the tree a unique aesthetic.
Those ones, Kent could already sense the edible smell coming from them.
[This is the Bloodline Skill Tree.
It is something of a myth, rumoured to have existed only among the Six True Primordials.
It houses all the bloodline skills there are, and learning those skills is as simple as eating a fruit.]
"Hold on a minute, Tower." Kent took a deep gulp and slowly processed what Tower had said.
He needed his clarity for what he was about to digest.

"You mean to say this tree standing before me, with over five thousand fruits on its branches, is a tree holding all the innate bloodline abilities I can awaken and use simply by eating mere ripped fruits?"
[Among other things, yes.]
"Among other things?" Kent gave the tower the "hold it there, girl" stance and asked, "Is there something else hidden that I should know?"
[As a matter of fact, yes.
While the master is not yet aware, a person, no matter how monstrous, can have no more than 500 innate bloodline skills.
Not even True Primordials had more than that...]
Kent looked at the Bloodline Skill Tree and counted over 5,000 fruits, meaning he has over 5,000 innate bloodline skills he can learn the moment the fruits are ripe.

If he were to take what Tower had just said into consideration, then it might seem he had just broken the innate bloodline ability scale by awakening the potential to unlock over 5,000 innate bloodline skills.
That is just mind-blowing, and he is well aware of that.
Unless, of course, there is something hidden beneath the surface.
Naturally, Kent immediately unearthed that something.
"I am guessing this many fruits have something to do with my many reincarnations and the Six True Primordials."
[Yes, Master.

The master had lived 13 lives, so it seems all innate talents linked to those lives have now manifested in this Bloodline Skill Tree, and as such, the master can learn them all by eating the ripe fruit.
Of course, the master may see it as too many innate skills considering the many fruits.
After all, once one keeps growing in the path of ascension, the skills they learned as mortals would become ineffective when they become immortals.
This means they would be forced to learn stronger ones.
However, the master shouldn’t worry since bloodline skills aren’t graded like external techniques.
These ones grow with the bloodline, so the stronger the bloodline becomes, the more advanced the skills.
In other words, learning an innate skill today is for life.
Also, an innate bloodline skill can evolve other learned innate skills, transforming them into something else.
So it can be that you will only learn 100 skills from this tree, but the others would superimpose on those 100 learned skills, making them more advanced and extremely powerful.]

"Well, when you put it that way, I guess I have not only become more powerful now, knowing I have a skill tree standing inside my Soul Sea, but I have the potential to learn over 5,000 innate bloodline skills."
Kent giggled like a child, feeling very happy he had landed this opportunity.
It is indeed a great opportunity for someone like him.
At this rate, worrying about learning other skills won’t be a problem.
It is as simple as plucking a fruit from a branch and eating it.
What could be easier than that?
He wouldn’t have to find a stronger version of a skill after the previous one had become less effective.
With just one, he could do more.
Kent keeps smiling; however, he suddenly furrowed his brow as if something important had just crossed his mind.
"Hold on a minute, Tower.
You said this is a Bloodline Skill Tree, right?
That I will awaken bloodline-related skills.
You also said that this tree houses all the innate bloodline skills tied to my many lives and those of the Six True Primordials.
If that is the case, does it mean I would have to awaken all 13 bloodlines and the six bloodlines that once belonged to the Six True Primordials before I can use them?"
Kent knew there had to be a catch.
If a skill is tied to one’s bloodline, then since he only has the Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline, does that mean he is only limited to the skills tied to that bloodline?
Obviously, he is missing something.
There is no way he would be given something only to lock it away from him due to an error.
[The master is the Chaos Dragon, and he would always be the Chaos Dragon.
This means he would only ever have the Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline.
However, that doesn’t mean the master wouldn’t be able to wield other bloodline skills.]
"How?"
[The master didn’t ask, so I said nothing.
However, the 13-layered discs and the six-orb disc, I believe, are connected to this skill tree.
The first one is called the 13 Layered Life Discs, which requires Life keys to unlock its power.
I believe the master would obtain those by reviewing all the memories of his past lives.
The second one is the Six Mark Fate Disc.
For that, the master would have to ask any of the True Primordials when he meets them again.]
And that answered his questions.
It seems, aside from his bloodline, there are other ways to harness the bloodline abilities of other incarnations and even the True Primordials.
That seems convenient for him, meaning he would now have to figure out what he had to do to unlock the 13 discs.
But for now, just knowing there is a way to harness those innate bloodline abilities is enough.
So far, aside from the [Chaos Aura] and [Chaos Dragon Scale] bloodline skills he had awakened, he is basically a brute without any refined skills to tap into when using his dragon form.
He had also forgone the use of the [Blood Chaos Aura] for now since he knew from Chaos that using that mutated aura would largely depend on his [Chaos Heart], which he had yet to form.
So in reality, he needs more skills tied to his bloodline than anything else. ’I wonder if by now walking the Blood & Slaughter path, my bloodline would also undergo mutation?’

It is always good if the results speak for themselves.

[That is true.
The master must handle that.
We, after all, still have temple masters to kill and more missions to go on.]
"Okay then," Kent reached and plucked one of the ripe fruits.

chapters.title: Chapter 1304: Chaos Scale Shield
paragraphs: "Smells like an apple." Kent sniffed the fruit. "I wonder if it would taste like one."
Obviously, Kent couldn’t wait long enough to taste it. His gluttony knows no bounds. So he placed it in his mouth and bit into it, taking a rather large chunk.
"Mmmmhhh, just like an apple." He savoured the taste, letting it slowly spread through his mouth and down his stomach. He quickly added the remaining half of the fruit.
In no time, he had devoured the whole fruit. However, to his disappointment, he only chewed for a fraction of a second since the fruit betrayed him by dissolving.
Although this is his soul sea, he expected to at least have the moment to further taste the fruit, feel the texture in his teeth and let the chewing take him to places he had never been before.
But that was cut short.
[The master could have just placed the fruit in his mouth, and it would have dissolved. No need to bite and attempt to chew.]
"Tsk," Kent said nothing but only waited for the essence in the fruit to take effect. The Tower seem to be growing stubborn lately.
Soon, however, the effect of eating the fruit happened as he expected. A green panel flashed across his vision.
[Congratulations on awakening an Innate Bloodline Skill. Name: Chaos Scale Shield]
Kent stared at the message with a calm expression for a few minutes before, like a child, he exclaimed happily.
"YESSSSSS!"

He almost jumped up from sheer excitement reading the message before him. Obviously, what he had received was something he most certainly was looking forward to, even if he didn’t know what would come today.
He had no idea what innate bloodline skill was contained in any of the fruits, not even Tower did, so he merely ate it and hoped for the best.
However, now it seems the skill he had received is something he was actually thrilled to have awakened.
Naturally, his exicitement run deeper than he is letting on. He, after all, had used this innate skill before.
He had seen what the [Chaos Scale Shield] is capable of from the memories of the Chaos Dragon.

Back then, when he buried Elina and reverted to his cold, chaotic self, he ventured into the Blood System, where his ascension to become one of the strongest people to ever appear during the Primordial Era began.
Chaos wanted to accomplish many things before leaving the Blood System.
One of those things was shedding his scale.
However, to do that, he must form his Chaos Heart, which, from what he knew, would call down the first Dragon Tribulation.
Passing that tribulation would finally allow him to shed his scales and form new ones.
However, from what he learned about Dragon Tribulation, the stronger the dragon, the more dangerous their tribulation — and well, Chaos was the strongest of them, so he knew he had to prepare.
It was through preparation that he awakened the defensive skill he would use for the rest of his stay in the Blood System and for the rest of his life.
That shield had broken the resolve of many tanks/brutes, and it had saved him countless times. That shield is the Chaos Scale Shield, an innate defensive skill.
[Name: Chaos Scale Shield]
[Grade: Innate]
[Mastery: Perfection+]
[Description: Shield formed from the reinforced scales of the Primordial Chaos Dragon...]

"Vague as ever, but this is what makes it fun and overpowered." Kent extended his hand, and triangular golden scales with red runes littering their surfaces appeared and began stacking themselves, forming a large shield.
His mastery is Perfection+ thanks to Chaos.
At first, it formed into a triangle-shaped shield. Then it reformed into a square, a rectangle, a pentagon, a hexagon, and many other shapes.
It reformed into any shape Kent wanted and could envision.
"Flawless as ever."
The brat was super happy, and that could be seen from the way he was manipulating the scales to form crazy-shaped shields.

"Oh, the look on that mountain king’s face was when his axe broke from a single attack to the Chaos Scale Shield." Kent laughed, imagining the horrified, stunned, and impressed expression that appeared on a certain mountain king’s face.
When this Mountain King heard Chaos was rampaging through the Blood System, he became pissed that someone was stealing the spotlight from him.
So, with his overinflated ego, he came challenging Chaos to a death duel, only for him to break his weapon on the first attack.
In the end, Chaos let him go. Later, they met again, but instead of challenging Chaos again, he tried to suck up to him.
Chaos, of course, had no intention of giving him any attention since he was on a mission.
"I wonder if that bastard survived the Primordial Era. It would be good to break his resolve again. Ah, what a sight that would be."

Far away in an unknown ruin, locked in a cave reinforced by a Tier 89 formation, a burly man sneezes, his expression cold... "As if my situation isn’t pitiful already, some bastard out there is already plotting against me."

He turns and looks at a series of paintings on the wall, and a pale smile appears on his face. "We will meet again, old friend. I hope you are still the same as before." He grinned and added, "Ah, what a sight that would be after I shatter that shield of yours...finally"
SNEEZE
Kent also sneezed, feeling a chill run down his spine. "Tsk, I wonder which bastard is plotting against me."
He wipes the idea from his mind and continues to transform his shield instead.
After he had had enough, he formed a single seal, and the scales flew and merged with his body. At once, his cloak-like armour transformed into dragon armour with a stylish reddish-gold design.
"Still the most beautiful armour there is." Kent grinned.
Even if it isn’t, considering the Soul Sentinel was crowned as the one with the most beautiful armour in the universe, as long as it makes him happy, the Chaos Dragon has the most beautiful armour.
But while he is exaggerating the beauty of his armour, looking at the armour that still feels like cotton but now has the pattern of a dragon, one can tell it is indeed beautiful and very powerful.
Kent summoned 1000 blood runes and made them merge with the armour. The moment they did, he felt like he had become indestructible.
One thing that made the Chaos Scale Shield indestructible is the fact that he can merge the blood runes with it, creating a rather overpowered augmentation.
"This also means I can augment Gaap with both the Chaos Scale Shield and the blood runes. There are even my dragon claws... As long as it is soul-linked to me, the sky is the limit."

Kent turned and looked at the Bloodline Skill Tree, and a smile formed on his lips. "This is the best gift for my first time plucking a fruit from you. I only ask one thing, and that is to keep blessing me with overpowered skills."
[Congratulations to the master. Now, I think the master is ready for the temple masters. I, for one, would love to see this skill at play.]
"Same here, Tower."
Kent deactivated the Chaos Scale Shield and reached for the second ripped fruit.

chapters.title: Chapter 1305: Blood Calamity Fist
paragraphs: Even though Kent knew the apple would dissolve when he placed it in his mouth, out of habit, he still bit into it and savoured the taste as it melted in his mouth.
"Still tastes great."
If the Tower were a person, she would have given him a deadpan expression. But Kent would have probably shrugged and focused on the message that appeared before his view.
He is shameless by nature. It is in his bloodline.
[Congratulations on awakening an Innate Bloodline Skill. Name: Blood Calamity Fist]
"Hmmm, looks like my assumption is right. My path as a blood cultivator had affected my bloodline, and as such, I have awakened a blood-related innate skill."
Although Chaos also cultivated the [Slaughter King Manual] as his cultivation method, he hadn’t awakened this innate skill — at least so far in his memories of that life.
However, Kent is now aware that his blood path is affecting his bloodline, and while that can be considered dangerous, Kent knows he has nothing to worry about.
If anything, this is a good thing. At least his path isn’t interfering with his bloodline, something that has killed or crippled many legendary cultivators.
A slight deviation from one’s cultivation path can cause irreversible damage.
But if that is the case, then this means he had to master this new skill to perfection by himself since Chaos hadn’t done that for him.
However, to be sure, he first checked the skill’s details.
[Name: Blood Calamity Fist]
[Grade: Innate]
[Mastery: Beginner]
[Description: Harness Blood Qi into a deadly fist...]
"Fuck, I hate you, Chaos," Kent smirked, looking at his mastery level still at the beginner stage. It is pitifully low for someone as awesome and handsome as him.
Every skill or technique has five levels of mastery.
Mastery Levels: Beginner ↠ Adept ↠ Intermediate ↠ Advanced ↠ Perfection.

If one’s perfection is on another level, they get a new rank called Perfection+. It is uncommon because most people take several years just to attain Perfection. Talking about Perfection+ is just too much of a stretch.
But seeing his mastery at the beginner stage made Kent curse Chaos for not awakening this innate bloodline skill and mastering it to perfection in the memories he had awakened so far.
Of course, he knew he had to work hard too, so he quickly snapped back to reality and checked the description again.
"Vague, just like the first one. However, vague things often turn out to be full of surprises."
"Let me try it and see what it is capable of."

Kent tapped into the Blood Calamity Fist, and at once, he felt the blood sea move and begin to form into a fist. In no time, a head-sized fist formed, looking more watery than something meant to injure or instil fear in the enemy.
"Lol, this is rather pitiful." Kent punched forward, and the fist moved. However, he knew it wouldn’t kill a Root Saint, much less injure them.
It is just too weak to make a difference.
"Again." He tapped into the skill again to form a new fist. However, this time he tried to make it more solid, since the previous watery look hadn’t satisfied him.
The mighty name of the skill even made it look pitiful.
So he envisioned a more solid fist and formed it. The size remained the same, but it was much more solid than the previous one.
[You have reached Level 2 beginner mastery]
"Oh, that is convenient." Kent punched forward again, and the fist exploded forward. This time, he knew if it struck a Saint, they would feel something.

It had levelled up his mastery to Level 2, which showed he had made the right move, and it counted. However, since this was the first time he was mastering a skill at the beginner stage, he felt he needed to do more.
Beginner wouldn’t cut it for him, not when he was going up against potential immortals. Thus, he locked in and started trying to make the blood fist more solid, neglecting the size.
It didn’t take long for the results to start to show.
[You have reached Level 3 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 4 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 5 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 9 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 1 Adept Mastery]
Kent continued to go on, making the fist more solid for a while, moving through the minor levels of the Adept mastery stage to the Intermediate stage.

However, the moment he reached the Intermediate stage, the solidification process method stopped working. The fist did become more solid, so much so that even a Spirit King would have to use defence to be able to withstand it.
He also found that the more solid the fist became, the faster it moved when he punched it forward. Naturally, that is what made it dangerous.
However, with solidification halted, he began to focus on size. He knew the bigger it got, the more or less solid it would become. In essence, to master this skill, he only needed to do two things.
Make it big and more solid.
As to how big and solid it could get, Kent decided to find out, so, not minding the passing of time, he started practising the skill inside his soul sea.
The moment he left seclusion, his destination would be the Void Temple, so it was best if he could master this skill to a level he could depend on in the upcoming battles.
Days passed, and aside from making the fist bigger and more solid, Kent did nothing else. Soon, he had turned the fist to the size of a mini mountain, solid as blood steel.
However, to Kent, anything but Perfection was not something he would accept, so he kept going. And after 30 days, he reached the level of Perfection.
[You have reached Level 1 Perfect Mastery]
In the air, a huge, solid red fist with a metallic shine hovered, casting a shadow over the blood sea.
"Now, this is something that can invoke the fear of god in the heart of even immortals," Kent grinned and punched forward. The giant fist moved and struck the blood sea, separating the water in half.
"Damn, that is awesome."

"Now, let me try augmenting it with the blood runes." Kent formed the Blood Calamity Fist again and summoned 1000 blood runes. While mastering it, he was also thinking of ways to make it even more powerful.
The answer that came to mind is the blood runes.
He commanded them to merge with the fist. The blood runes started merging to various sides of the fist, instantly increasing the danger level.
COUGH
Just when the first 100 entered the First, Kent felt his soul pressed by something extremely dangerous. He opened his eyes on the outside, spitting out a mouthful of blood.
"Well, I am not doing that again," Kent sighed in resignation. The idea to augment the Blood Calamity Fist came from the Chaos Shield, since he was able to augment that.
Now, he tried, and his soul was nearly injured.
"I can add at least 50. Better to be safe than sorry." Still, he hadn’t wanted to ignore the prospect of adding that augmentation.

"I wonder if I can augment it with the Chaos Scales." A grin formed on his lips, but he didn’t go ahead with that thought. Injuring his soul isn’t something he wants to do at this point in his mission.
"Okay then, time to go kick ass."

[You have reached Level 4 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 5 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 9 beginner mastery]
[You have reached Level 1 Adept Mastery]
Kent continued to go on, making the fist more solid for a while, moving through the minor levels of the Adept mastery stage to the Intermediate stage.
However, the moment he reached the Intermediate stage, the solidification process method stopped working.
The fist did become more solid, so much so that even a Spirit King would have to use defence to be able to withstand it.
He also found that the more solid the fist became, the faster it moved when he punched it forward.
Naturally, that is what made it dangerous.
However, with solidification halted, he began to focus on size.
He knew the bigger it got, the more or less solid it would become.
In essence, to master this skill, he only needed to do two things.
Make it big and more solid.
As to how big and solid it could get, Kent decided to find out, so, not minding the passing of time, he started practising the skill inside his soul sea.
The moment he left seclusion, his destination would be the Void Temple, so it was best if he could master this skill to a level he could depend on in the upcoming battles.
Days passed, and aside from making the fist bigger and more solid, Kent did nothing else.
Soon, he had turned the fist to the size of a mini mountain, solid as blood steel.
However, to Kent, anything but Perfection was not something he would accept, so he kept going.
And after 30 days, he reached the level of Perfection.
[You have reached Level 1 Perfect Mastery]
In the air, a huge, solid red fist with a metallic shine hovered, casting a shadow over the blood sea.
"Now, this is something that can invoke the fear of god in the heart of even immortals," Kent grinned and punched forward.
The giant fist moved and struck the blood sea, separating the water in half.
"Damn, that is awesome."
"Now, let me try augmenting it with the blood runes." Kent formed the Blood Calamity Fist again and summoned 1000 blood runes.
While mastering it, he was also thinking of ways to make it even more powerful.
The answer that came to mind is the blood runes.
He commanded them to merge with the fist.
The blood runes started merging to various sides of the fist, instantly increasing the danger level.
COUGH
Just when the first 100 entered the First, Kent felt his soul pressed by something extremely dangerous.
He opened his eyes on the outside, spitting out a mouthful of blood.
"Well, I am not doing that again," Kent sighed in resignation.
The idea to augment the Blood Calamity Fist came from the Chaos Shield, since he was able to augment that.
Now, he tried, and his soul was nearly injured.
"I can add at least 50.
Better to be safe than sorry." Still, he hadn’t wanted to ignore the prospect of adding that augmentation.
"I wonder if I can augment it with the Chaos Scales." A grin formed on his lips, but he didn’t go ahead with that thought.
Injuring his soul isn’t something he wants to do at this point in his mission.
"Okay then, time to go kick ass."

chapters.title: Chapter 1306: Vhar’Zeth, the first Temple Master
paragraphs: The moment Kent stepped out of the Ice fortress he built for his short seclusion, it crumbled. Gaap floated down, his expression calm as he scanned Kent for a few seconds before he smiled.
"Looks like you have reached a milestone, Master. Congratulations."
Kent smiled and nodded, "Thank you, Gaap. I have indeed made big progress this time. But so did you. I can feel the changes."
"I didn’t sit idle either. Although I couldn’t break the first seal since we are still in a high world, I managed to form a Resentful Tattoo that lets me tap into 30% of the first seal’s powers.
I believe that will be enough for the adventure ahead of us." Gaap said with an enthusiastic smile. He is thrilled and ready for the adventure ahead.
He is a living sword that had once fought in an era-ending battle, so obviously, just 30% of his first sealed power isn’t going to be small.
Kent may not want to say it, but whenever he wields Gaap, the hidden power he feels buried deep within him is just terrifying. He said he had 9 seals to break as he continues to grow.
So Kent is ready to see what he has in store for him.
With the two of them working together, the next battles ahead of them would be much more manageable. Kent had become a monster in his own right, so he was ready for anything.
"That is good to hear. In any case, we have to move. The faster we clear the temple, the better," Gaap nodded, and they started flying toward the Void Temple.
During the ten days of massacre, he passed by the Void Temple, so he knew where to go now.
Although it isn’t within the scan radius of his soul map, the moment they moved for 5 minutes, Kent saw the temple. However, he didn’t teleport to it.
They took their dear time and flew to it.
After a few more minutes, they arrived at the red pagoda.
"Looks beautiful for a void temple," Gaap said, his expression calm. The pagoda stood majestically, the power of the void oozing off it.
If one is not aware, they would think it is a treasure, but once they enter, they would know it is anything but a treasure. The horrors hidden within it are no joke.

Kent didn’t know much about the Void Temple masters hidden in this particular Void Temple. However, he had already ranked them as some of the most powerful beings during the Primordial Era, so he is prepared for anything.
But then again, what he didn’t know was that the temple masters are like criminals in the Void Beast Race, sent to somehow contribute to the cause of the Void Beasts.
They aren’t their best; however, many succeeded, and many also died at the claws of the Chaos Dragon and a few brave others.
Now, it seems they would be meeting him again, and this time, Kent plans to make it his mission to go after them before they cause too much damage.
The invasion of the Void Beast is destined to happen; however, he would not allow the criminals of the Void Beast Race to run rampant in his universe.
"There is a chance the moment we enter, we would be attacked, so be ready," Kent said to Gaap, who nodded and transformed into his sword form.
Kent grabbed hold of him and slowly started walking toward the entrance leading to the first floor of the void temple.
A few seconds later, he stood at the entrance, his expression calm. He had done this many times before, but that doesn’t mean it was fun.
"Maybe I would enjoy it this time around."
After taking a deep breath, Kent walked through and appeared on scorched earth. The moment he walked through the door, he found himself standing at the centre of a lava sea.
"Well, that is also one way to start things..." Kent looked around, but aside from the sea of lava, there was nothing else in sight.
"Strange, they usually attack the moment you appear. They’ve nearly killed me a few times in the past with that move. So why is the temple master not here?"
Kent became puzzled.
What he knew from the Primordial Era had proven to be wrong this time around. The attack he anticipated never came. That wasn’t how he remembered the Void Beasts, so this took him by surprise.
However, he didn’t let it get to him. He opened the soul map, and the 80,000 km appeared within his sensing range.
All around, he saw nothing but a sea of lava. However, he also saw something akin to a trail which led west.
So he teleported to the edge of his soul map toward the west and, expanding the sensing range again, saw dry ground, though lava channels ran everywhere.
"If I am not mistaken, this is a Primordial Void Flame. If I get some more flame treasures, I am sure forming my second flame core wouldn’t be too hard."
[That is indeed true. However, the master must first clear the temple of all dangers before he can do that.]

Kent is, of course, aware of that, so he started moving in the direction of the dried ground. After teleporting five more times, Kent saw who he had come for, seated on a flaming throne, his gaze burning in an unholy radiance.
He is about 4 meters tall and has obsidian skin split by molten void-flame veins. A deadly flaming scythe rested on the back of his flame throne, his gaze locked on Kent.
"You are finally here," he asked, his expression burning like a tsunami.
"Took me a minute, but I am indeed here. I have, after all, entered this godforsaken place for you ugly bastards."
"So you know who I am." There seems to be a hint of surprise in his flame-lit eyes. They, after all, are Void Beasts, so he never expected someone in this era to be aware of their existence.
They only existed during the Primordial Era.

"There is no way I wouldn’t know who you are, fella. I have always dreamt of when you losers would show up again. I mean, after you were miserably defeated and driven away like a bunch of losers the last time."
BOOM
The taunt got to the temple master, so his fury exploded, causing the space around him to burst into flames. Lava gushed out, spraying all around.
"No need to throw a tantrum. I doubt you were even born back then. But even if you were, considering how pitiful your people were back then, you would have died like a bug, crashed like a nut.
So be grateful for that. However, since you are here, then despair, for I have come to do what we couldn’t during the Primordial Era."
BOOM
Kent’s own killing intent exploded, and at once, the air inside the first floor of the void temple turned grim. Kent’s new and improved killing intent had already reached a whole new level.
"I, Vhar’Zeth, the first temple master of fire, will slay you and use your blood to—"
"Cut the shit, bastard." Kent arrived in front of him and struck with his sword. With danger coming, Vhar’Zeth was forced to keep his mouth shut and retaliate.
BOOM
He was sent flying, his flaming scythe flying out from his hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 1307: Resentful Slash
paragraphs: The moment their weapons met, Vhar’Zeth felt his hand tremble, a wave of pain vibrating through them as if he had just met the attack of a god.
This forced the weapon out of his hand, and his body was hurled back, crashing through his flaming throne, shattering it in the process.
In a fraction of a second, his majestic throne was shattered completely.
Kent is already aware that the throne was merely forged from the flame (magma) in the region, making it something that can be replaced easily.
But shattering the symbol of his authority inside the domain he controls is just too disrespectful.

However, being sent rolling and crashing through boulders and stones sure was humbling. His ego was bruised, but he learned a bitter lesson... ’never act arrogant in front of the primordial chaos dragon’
Kent watches him roll and crash through the flaming environment for a few hundred km before coming to a stop. He stood up, and his body exploded with power.
He is pissed, and it shows on his face.
"Oh, so you are a Root Immortal, huh?"
He hid his cultivation base at first so much that even the Tower couldn’t discern it. However, now he can see and sense it. Even better, he had two immortal qi, making him even more dangerous.
He extended his hand, and his scythe flew into his grip. That one wasn’t destroyed, a sign that the scythe is at least real, unlike the throne that was shattered into rubble.
"Void Inferno Body."

With no delay, Vhar’Zeth lunged at Kent, his body increasing in size along with his weapon. By the time he reached Kent and his weapon came down on Kent, he had risen to 8 meters, his scythe a giant weapon worthy of its name.
It cast a shadow over Kent; however, even without his void wings, he saw the attack coming. Half his flame veins activated, allowing him to move at a terribly fast pace.
Kent didn’t run away; he instead jumped on the scythe and, using his speed, ran along the jagged handle of the scythe, unleashing a three-sword arc.
The attacks landed on Vhar’Zeth’s face, throwing his head back. He had no time to defend; however, his skin is also thick enough to tank those three sword arcs.
Seeing this, Kent summoned 300 spears and sent all flying toward his face.
The attack was sudden, and while he would love to defend against them with his stony face, the moment they arrived, he found himself staring at 300 spears, each a deadly weapon.
His two immortal qi activated, manifesting a shield on his face. Thankfully, the shield forced the three hundred spears to a halt. Then they ignited, turning to ash.
However, Kent didn’t care about the sudden loss of his three hundred weapons. If anything, he was more thrilled that Vhar’Zeth used his immortal qi to shield his face.
The moment he made that action, Kent tapped into the soul map and teleported to the ground, moved 2 km away and unleashed the Void Cleave sword attack.
The 100-meter-long crescent sword arc appeared, and as it moved through the air, it started gathering momentum.
That sword attack depends on the distance between him and his target.
2 km isn’t much to make it a deadly blow; however, it is also strong enough to accomplish what Kent wanted.
Vhar’Zeth had now become a 10-meter-tall flaming giant with a jagged body. He seemed to have grown bigger, and his body was made from what appeared to be hardened magma.
His scythe is now 15 meters long, and the curved end of the blade is lit on a compressed flame, possibly a condensed primordial void flame.
However, while his strength is bone-shattering now, his speed was sacrificed, making him much slower.

However, while speed is important in combat, Kent knew that with a single blow, a large chunk of the battlefield would be gone. Vhar’Zeth’s strength increases with his body size. The bigger he gets, the stronger he becomes.
So Kent knew best not to compete in the strength department. Meeting a brute in his first challenge was good. This would allow him to run circles around him and see just how much Gaap had grown.
So sacrificing 300 spears for an attack isn’t a waste. In fact, the moment Vhar’Zeth sensed the void cleave attack, it was already before him.
ROAR
He roared at the top of his voice, crossing his hands before him. A shield of void energy manifested around the cross he formed, causing the attack to land on it with a devastating boom.
The recoil pushed Vhar’Zeth back a few steps, throwing dust and smoke into the air. It was just 2 km, so there was not much damage.
However, the moment the attack landed on Vhar’Zeth, he sensed he had been played.
He may be a brute, but he is not stupid.
When he destroyed the 300 spears, he sensed something was amiss. There was no way someone would send that many weapons just to be destroyed.

Kent didn’t even attack with it as he should have. If anything, he merely sent them flying at his face to test something. But Vhar’Zeth had fought many battles, and judging by the attack from Kent’s first slash, he sensed something terrible was amiss.
Nobody that powerful could just let 300 of their weapons be destroyed like they were made of paper.
However, before he could address that discovery, the void cleave arrived, and like with the sword, he also sensed the conspiracy.
Like with the spears, Kent had the chance to attack more powerfully. However, he merely scratched him, and that was just not a coincidence. This made him panic...
However, he was made aware of just what kind of monster Kent is right after the void cleave was defended.
Up in the air, he heard howling, roaring, screaming, and wailing. He quickly waved his hand to clear the smoke so he could see what had happened.
When the smoke cleared, and he saw the sight before him, his stony face turned pale.
Up in the air, Kent stood, his 2-meter-long jagged sword raised, thousands of resentful souls screaming and howling as they were absorbed into the dark obsidian steel blade.
"Allow me to test this on you." Kent’s blood sword aura ignited, and at once, all resentful souls were absorbed into the sword.
RUMBLE
The sky rumbled, clouds turning dark in an instant. Vhar’Zeth immediately formed a shield by stabbing his scythe into the ground, manifesting a stack of rocky shields.
However, Kent didn’t mind. In fact, this made him even more giddy.
"Resentful Slash."

With a roar, his sword fell in a rather powerful vertical slash, manifesting a 100-meter-long black crescent sword arc. Painful screams and howling followed the slash as it quickly arrived before Vhar’Zeth’s shield.
SHRNNNNK
That was the sound made before the resentful sword arc sped away, cutting the very ground in half, travelling several thousand km deep.
For a moment, there was no movement from Vhar’Zeth.
But then a small wind from the attack that cut the ground blew, and the shield separated in half, and along with it, half of Vhar’Zeth’s body fell to the left while the other half fell to the right.
THUD THUD
They crashed to the ground. His blood flew like a river, sizzling on the ground.
Just like that, Kent had killed one of the five void temple masters, the temple master of fire.

He merely wanted to test Gaap at his peak, only to learn he had used 5% of his power. That is shocking, and Kent is already wondering just what the 30% would be capable of.
"I only used 5%, and with enough time, I can recover that percentage. However, to fully unleash all 30%, you would need to at least have a three-second window."
Kent nodded.
Three seconds sounded like a short time, but in a battle against an immortal, 3 seconds is very long. A lot can happen in a second, much less three seconds.

The attack he had used just now happened in less than a second, just a little over 0.5 seconds. But even so, Vhar’Zeth was able to harness both his immortal qi to form a defence that would have blocked a Void Cleave unleashed from 8 km away.
This means Kent would have to create favourable conditions that would buy him at least 3 seconds if he wants to see how much stronger Gaap has become.
Of course, he would think of doing that when he meets the right conditions. For now, the stronger he becomes, the shorter the time he would need to unleash more of Gaap’s power.
"How long do you need to recover?" Kent asked.
"About 10 days tops. I have quite a lot of resentful souls stored away, so give me ten days."
"Okay. Get to it, I have to explore this place anyway." Gaap nodded and started recovering. He wants to be useful throughout the mission, so he quickly went to work.
Kent, too, wasn’t about to let go of a chance to see what he could find here.
The flame inside the region is a Primordial Flame. It is at least a high-grade Primordial Flame, so he wants to see if there is more to it than what he is seeing.
The floor master is dead, and as such, he is the new owner. That can even be confirmed by the messages he had received.
[You have killed the first temple master, Vhar’Zeth]
[You have received the first temple Key.]
[Collect all five keys and become the owner of the Void Temple.]
Things had indeed changed. During Chaos’s time, clearing the temple is just it. There were no added benefits after clearing every floor.
In fact, every temple cleared vanishes, never to be seen again.
However, now it seems he would receive the temple as a gift after clearing all five floors.

Kent welcomed the change since it would benefit him. The first floor would benefit his flame cultivation, so at least that is a boon. He would see what the other floors have to offer when he gets there.
Kent walked to Vhar’Zeth’s body and waved his hand, taking his core and scythe. There was also a pouch hanging from his waist, so he took it and quickly looked inside.
There are only three things inside...
"A tome, Blood Essence and Talisman."
Kent reached into the pouch and pulled out the three items. There is a strange kind of energy around them that makes Kent immediately sense that something is amiss.
However, since Vhar’Zeth is dead, he didn’t place much focus on that and chose to see what the three things are. However, he had measures in place just in case.
’Tower, I forgot to ask, but can the temple masters on the other floors see what is happening here?’
[They did. However, the moment you obtained the first key, they all became blind to see on this floor.]
’Good.’
If he were being spied on, he wouldn’t have done anything to the tome since it is a void-related technique.
Kent isn’t yet affined with the void. However, he knew he would gain that affinity as he used the Jade Void Wings.
Because of that, he wouldn’t want the others destroying their tomes. Of course, he somehow does not think they would destroy them, since they may have this assumption that they can kill him.
Vhar’Zeth did, and now he is dead. But Void Beasts are arrogant by nature.
There is also an issue with the language. However, hearing Kent speak fluently with Vhar’Zeth made them see him as a threat.
Only a few people can speak their language, and all of them fell during the Primordial Era. So Kent is a threat, and they most certainly would not tolerate his existence.
Either way, they weren’t about to bet on that.
The tome has a worn-out look. It seems to be made from a stone-like material, a strange kind of energy coating it.
There are some inscriptions on it in the Aelthryn runic alphabet.
"Three Step Void Prison," Kent read the name of the technique imbued into this tome.
Although he cannot learn it yet, the moment he is done cultivating the first form of the [Void Drive] technique to perfection, he will gain Void Affinity.
The moment he obtains that, he will be able to learn it.
He didn’t know much about the technique, but he could tell it was a technique that could be used to trap others inside the void.
Although he doubted it would be very effective against Void Beasts, he knew that with enough mastery of the void, he could use it against them.
They are Void Beasts, but that doesn’t mean they are superior in terms of void mastery. So he can only store this away for now and wait for when he can actually use it.
"Ingrid and Arien would benefit from it, too. They both have an affinity for the void energy, so I guess I will share it with them when I go back."
Kent paused from examining the remaining two items and let his mind wander to the thought of his wives. It’s been a while since he saw them.
He is aware they are now inside the Planet Killer Dungeon.

However, instead of heading to the 5th floor, they decided to look around the 4th floor some more. Later, Unity found something that brought back past memories, causing her to enter a trance-like state.
So they chose to wait for her there, and so for the past month, they had been staying there.
"I wonder if they are now ready to challenge the 5th floor."
After a few more thoughts, he focused back on the two items he retrieved from Vhar’Zeth’s storage pouch.

chapters.title: Chapter 1309: Talisman
paragraphs: "Hmm, when I first saw it, I thought it was a blood essence," Kent said, closely examining the purple orb radiating intense energy.
While blood essence is golden in colour, Kent knew there were many beings out there with different colours. So he was really inclined to believe what he saw was a blood essence.
"Judging by how intense the energy coming out is and the fact that it feels similar to void essence, then this might be related to the void."
The tower couldn’t find a name for it, so he only assumed its vague nature and then stored it away. Since it is not blood essence, he would store it away.
He had only awoken 80,000 blood runes now, so he was hoping this would have pushed him further to awakening more. Too bad it’s something he can’t absorb just yet.
His focus turned to the talisman.
Seeing the triangular-shaped talisman, a hint of sadness washed over his mind. Back during the Primordial Era, talismans were a big deal...they still are.
One can encode their skills and techniques into talismans and, with enough mastery, even increase their power. Elemental attacks were a thing back then.
But aside from skills and techniques, many with creative minds can create powerful restrictions using a talisman.
Many gods, Supremes, and Celestials created talismans strong enough to kill multiple Void Beasts of their same rank at once.
Chaos met many warriors using the Talisman during his time in the Blood System and even developed a liking for it. Of course, his love for it originated from the time he spent with Elina.
She had always wanted to learn talisman inscription. Too bad she never got to learn it before her death.

Looking at this talisman brought back some sad memories. However, knowing that Elina is still alive and that he is doing everything to get to her made him wipe that sadness away and instead focus on the positive.
"I will take you to all the talisman festivals there are in the universe this time." With a smile on his face, he focused more on the talisman hovering before him.
"It is an attacking-type talisman for sure," Kent examined in some more detail, looking at the purple lines and symbols carved on it. He recognised most, but many eluded him.
In the end, he focused on the one person who could help him...
"Tower, what am I looking at?"
Instead of speaking, rows of text appeared before him showing the name, tier, type, and description of the talisman...
[Name: Purple Void Dragon Lightning Blast]
[Tier: 45 (Peak)]
[Type: Attack]
[Description: A talisman made to mimic the overwhelming lightning blast of a Purple Void Dragon. The greater the energy used to activate it, the stronger the output.]
"Oh, so a Divine Talisman made this." Kent didn’t know if he should be happy or thank his stars he had just escaped disaster.

The Talisman is Tier 45; naturally, it can be considered the same as a Tier 45 formation or an array. In the realm of talismans, just like formations, arrays, artisans, and many others, the ranking is counted in Tiers.
A talisman made by a Divine Talisman is between Tier 41 and 50 and strong enough to kill even an Immortal Lord when the right amount of energy is poured into it.

If Vhar’Zeth had used it against him, he would have suffered greatly. Even with his Chaos scale shield, he would have sustained some heavy damage. Perhaps the only reason Vhar’Zeth didn’t use it was the energy it would require to activate it.
He was afraid that if he used that much energy, even as a Root Immortal, he would have been drained. But again, why would he even use that when the battle lasted less than a minute?
But if he had indeed used it, perhaps Kent would have been in bad shape by now.
"Good thing he didn’t use it. However, I can’t help but wonder if the four remaining temple masters also have this and would be using it against me."
Moments like this, regardless of one’s strength, they can’t help but be cautious. Kent knew he had to be cautious, so he stored away the talisman and decided to focus on finding a counter for it.
He still has the tower shop with him. He would look through it and, hopefully, find something that, even if they used a Divine-level talisman against him, he would survive.
After handling that, he decided to go around the first floor to see if he could find something useful.
Learning that the flame on the floor is a Primordial Flame made him happy. It means he is a step closer to forming his second flame core.
He killed Vhar’Zeth too fast before he could show what he was made of. If he had lived long enough, Kent would have seen the power of the Primordial Void Flame.
Although not the strongest void flame out there, it is still strong enough, and with Vhar’Zeth having more time on his side, he would have unleashed catastrophic damage in the end.
Kent knew that, and so he went for the kill when he had the chance. Now, it is his to claim.
His first core was formed from hell flame. If he manages to form his second core from a void flame, then who knows what he would be capable of when he gains void affinity?
[Core of the universe]
Meanwhile, at the core of the universe, Lady Universe is hosting a viewing session for a few cosmic beings. On a screen at the moment, Kent is flying around the first floor of the Void Temple.
Present are cosmic manifestations of the Enchantress with her long hair sweeping the very floor, Fate smoking on his pipe, Karma wearing a straw hat, and Destiny sucking on a lollipop.
The moment Kent entered the Void Temple, they came hoping to see him kick ass—well, Karma came to see his ass kicked.
"Looks like he had everything figured out," Enchantress said, looking at Kent flying around.
"Indeed." Lady Universe nodded, "This can be considered his first battle with a standard immortal, but he killed it in less than a minute."
"He just got lucky," Karma smirked, turning his gaze away from the display screen.
The others just shook their heads.
They know Karma is merely throwing a tantrum. He knew Kent was needed for what was coming, but because of old grudges, he couldn’t help but hope Kent at least got stabbed in the chest once.
Destiny removed the lollipop from her cherry lips, creating a silent pop.
"I mean, if a mortal killing a Root Immortal with two immortals in less than a minute can be considered luck, then I want all the luck of the cosmos."

A giggling sound filled the core of the universe. They are all aware Destiny has a thing against Karma. The two often clash over the smallest thing, so when she saw the chance present itself, she took it.
Now, Karma could only glare at her with a furious expression.
However, a sigh escaped his lips, and instead, he started to wait for when Kent would enter the second floor and clash with the second-floor temple master.
